scenarios.title: Following Instructions at School
scenarios.domain: Expressing Ourselves and Connecting with Others

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can show comprehension of general information, specific information and instructions in short oral texts about daily events if spoken slowly and clearly.
specific_standards: Receptive: Follow clear instructions in learning activities.
Interactive: Execute multi-step directions in learning activities.
learning_outcomes: Can follow clear instructions in learning activities to complete a task (e.g., "First, cut the paper, then glue it on the flowchart.").
Can follow and respond to multi-step directions in-class activities (e.g., "You need to fold the paper before you cut it.").
Can respond appropriately to oral instructions (e.g., "Let's put away our books.").

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can extract general and specific information in simple texts on everyday familiar topics with or without visual support.
specific_standards: Reading: Show comprehension of written instructions for classroom activities.
Reading: Demonstrate comprehension of basic descriptions in texts.
Phonemic Awareness: Decode English graphemes and phonemes using knowledge of word parts, syllabification, and phonemic awareness.
learning_outcomes: Can show comprehension of written instructions for classroom activities by following them step-by-step (e.g., "I can cut and fold the paper.").
Can demonstrate comprehension of basic descriptions in texts by summarizing key details from reading materials (e.g., "The flowchart is colorful.").
Can recognize and divide compound and multi-syllabic words into syllables (e.g., "cardboard" into "card-board" and "instructional" into "in-struc-tion-al").

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can exchange personal information, descriptions of basic things, simple questions and answers, and simple directions.
specific_standards: Productive: Talk about simple rules and laws.
Interactive: Answer questions about their daily routine.
learning_outcomes: Can describe basic classroom rules related to school projects (e.g., "We must clean up after making the poster." "You have to wash your hands after using paint." "We should put away the scissors and glue when we're done.").

Can answer and ask follow-up questions to classmates about steps in a class project as part of their routine (e.g., "What do I do after cutting the paper?" "Glue it on the poster." "Where do I put the markers after using them?" "In the supply box.").
Can explain safety rules at school when using classroom materials (e.g., "You should use scissors carefully." "Always walk, don't run when carrying sharp objects.").

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can create short, organized texts on familiar topics, incorporating revisions and feedback to improve clarity.
specific_standards: Productive: Write thank-you cards.
Interactive: Respond to written questions about a class reading assignment.
learning_outcomes: Can write a simple thank-you card to a classmate or teacher for helping with a class project (e.g., "Thank you for helping me cut the paper for the poster.").
Can answer simple written questions about steps in a class project (e.g., "What did you cut?" "I cut the paper for the poster." "What did you use to glue the pictures?" "I used glue.").

Can write short answers about following instructions in class (e.g., "Where do we have to put the poster?" "On the wall in the classroom." "What did you do after cutting the paper?" "I glued it on the poster.").

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can utilize simplified language, visual aids, and step-by-step explanations to help peers engage with tasks and information.
specific_standards: Text: Contextualize simple school announcements according to local needs.
Text: Simplify textbook content for peers.
learning_outcomes: Can contextualize school announcements using gestures or visuals to highlight key details (e.g., pointing to Friday on a calendar and saying, "The poster event is on Friday." or showing a pair of scissors and saying, "We will make the poster tomorrow.").
Can simplify textbook content with basic words and visuals (e.g., pointing to a picture and saying, "This book is about instructions.").

Can simplify classroom instructions or textbook content for peers using simple words and visuals (e.g., showing a picture of scissors and paper and saying, "Cut the paper like this." or pointing to a step-by-step poster and saying, "First, cut the paper. Then, glue it on the poster.").

grammatical_features: Plural of the imperatives (e.g., "Let's make a poster.")
Sequencing words (e.g., "first, next")
Future tense (e.g., "I will make a mask." "I am going to make a mask.")

linguistic_competences.nouns: paper, scissors, glue, pencil, poster, classroom, teacher, project, mask, art, decoration, card, crayon, paint, cardboard, fabric, string, bead, flowchart
linguistic_competences.verbs: cut, fold, paste, draw, create, share, decorate, measure, write
linguistic_competences.adjectives: big, small, colorful, new, fun, sharp

vocabulary.pronunciation_and_phonemic_awareness: Pronunciation: /p/ in "poster" and /s/ in "scissors". Phonemic awareness: Recognition of compound words and syllable division (e.g., "classroom, class-room, two-syllables")
vocabulary.pragmatic_competences: Asking for clarification: "What do I need to do next?" Communicating future intentions: "I will make a hat!"
vocabulary.sociolinguistic_competences: Collaborating: Using imperatives and "let's" for group activities.

skills_and_technology_integration.skills: Instruction Giving: Using imperatives and sequencing words. Collaboration: Describing tasks in groups using collaborative language.
skills_and_technology_integration.technology_integration: Use video recording and editing tools for instructional videos and digital tools for flowchart creation.

projects.name: Project 1: Classroom How-To Guide
projects.overview: Students create a step-by-step written guide for a classroom task (e.g., organizing supplies, setting up for an activity), using imperatives and sequencing words like "first, next, and then".

projects.name: Project 2: Instructional Video
projects.overview: Students record a video demonstrating a classroom routine, such as cleaning up or preparing for a project, using imperatives and collaborative language like "let's" and "we".

projects.name: Project 3: Task Flowchart
projects.overview: Students design a flowchart outlining steps in completing a task (e.g., art project or science experiment) with sequencing words and imperatives.

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can show comprehension of general information, specific information and instructions in short oral texts about daily events if spoken slowly and clearly.
specific_standards: Receptive: Identify specific information in announcements or recordings.
Interactive: Ask for repetition and clarification in a conversation about known topics.
learning_outcomes: Can identify specific information in announcements about classroom tasks (e.g., "Team One sweeps the floor, and Team Two arranges the desks.").
Can ask for repetition and clarification in conversations about classroom tasks (e.g., "Can you repeat which team cleans the board?" "Can you say that again? Who arranges the desks?").
Can identify specific details in recordings about classroom cleaning activities (e.g., "We sweep the floor.").

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can extract general and specific information in simple texts on everyday familiar topics with or without visual support.
specific_standards: Reading: Extract specific information from short informational texts.
Reading: Demonstrate comprehension of basic descriptions in texts.
Phonemic Awareness: Decode English graphemes and phonemes using knowledge of word parts, syllabification, and phonemic awareness.
learning_outcomes: Can extract specific information from short informational texts about classroom chores (e.g., "We sweep the floor.").
Can demonstrate comprehension of basic text descriptions by discussing what each chore means (e.g., "Sweep means clean the floor with a broom.").
Can decode English graphemes and phonemes using knowledge of compound words and syllable division (e.g., recognizing "whiteboard" as "white-board" with two syllables).

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can exchange personal information, descriptions of basic things, simple questions and answers, and simple directions.
specific_standards: Productive: Give simple directions within the school.
Interactive: Participate in short conversations about familiar topics.
learning_outcomes: Can give simple directions to find places in the school (e.g., "The cleaning area is next to the bathroom.").
Can participate in short conversations about familiar tasks (e.g., "What are you doing?" "I am arranging the desks.").
Can ask and answer questions about their favorite activities (e.g., "Can you help me clean the classroom, please?" "Yes, I can clean up the board.").

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can create short, organized texts on familiar topics, incorporating revisions and feedback to improve clarity.
specific_standards: Productive: Create short descriptions of favorite characters from books.
Interactive: Draft questions for guest speakers, including imaginary "guests" or "characters" of relevance.
learning_outcomes: Can describe a character involved in classroom tasks (e.g., "My favorite character is Super Tidy. He always helps organize the desks and sweep the floor.").
Can write simple questions for guest speakers (e.g., "How can we keep our classroom clean?").
Can share their character description with the class (e.g., "Super Tidy likes to clean. He likes to sweep the floor and arrange the desks.").

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can utilize simplified language, visual aids, and step-by-step explanations to help peers engage with tasks and information.
specific_standards: Text: Explain simple written instructions to peers.
Communication: Facilitate discussions on classroom topics among peers.
learning_outcomes: Can explain written instructions with simple steps and gestures (e.g., "Please, wipe down the desks." and mimics wiping down the desks).
Can facilitate discussions by asking classmates questions, encouraging answers, and using gestures like nodding to prompt responses (e.g., "How can you help keep the classroom clean?").
Can summarize classroom responsibilities for peers, using basic words and gestures (e.g., "We put away our supplies." and points to a labeled supply bin).

grammatical_features: Present continuous (e.g., "We are sweeping.")
Imperatives (e.g., "Sweep." "Let's sweep.")
Modal "can" in affirmative and interrogative form (e.g., "I can sweep the floor." "Can you help me wipe down the desks?")

linguistic_competences.nouns: whiteboard, window, door, trash can, dustpan, mop, sponge, bucket, cloth, cleaner, cleaning supplies
linguistic_competences.verbs: sweep, wipe, arrange, organize, tidy, put away, clean up
linguistic_competences.adjectives: tidy, clean, organized, easy, messy, neat, dirty, busy, lazy

vocabulary.pronunciation_and_phonemic_awareness: Pronunciation: /r/ in "arrange" and /s/ in "supply". Phonemic awareness: Recognition of compound words and syllable division (e.g., "whiteboard, white-board, two syllables")
vocabulary.pragmatic_competences: Offering help: "Can I help you sweep?" Giving instructions: "Please arrange the chairs."
vocabulary.sociolinguistic_competences: Collaborating in class: Using "please" to maintain politeness in interactions when giving instructions, fostering inclusion and solidarity. (e.g., "Let's clean the classroom." "Sweep the floor, please.")

skills_and_technology_integration.skills: Responsibility: Assigning and describing cleaning tasks using imperatives. Communication: Using collaborative language and present continuous tense to describe cleaning actions.
skills_and_technology_integration.technology_integration: Use digital design tools for posters and charts.

projects.name: Project 1: Classroom Clean-Up Plan
projects.overview: Students develop a written plan outlining roles and responsibilities for keeping the classroom clean, using imperatives and present continuous tense (e.g., "We are sweeping the floors.").

projects.name: Project 2: Cleaning Instruction Poster
projects.overview: Students design posters with illustrated instructions for cleaning tasks, using imperatives and collaborative language (e.g., "Let's arrange the chairs.").

projects.name: Project 3: Classroom Responsibility Chart
projects.overview: Students create a responsibility chart on paper or digitally, assigning weekly tasks to classmates, using present continuous and imperatives.

scenarios.title: The Local Farm Stand
scenarios.domain: Expressing Ourselves and Connecting with Others

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can show comprehension of general information, specific information and instructions in short oral texts about daily events if spoken slowly and clearly.
specific_standards: Receptive: Identify specific information in announcements or recordings.
Interactive: Engage in simple discussions on lessons or current events.
learning_outcomes: Can identify specific items and their prices from announcements in the market (e.g., "Two papayas for three dollars." "This papaya costs two dollars.").
Can engage in simple discussions about items bought at the market (e.g., "I buy bananas.").
Can respond to questions about prices and quantities in role-play scenarios (e.g., "How much is the banana?" "It is six bananas for one dollar.").

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can extract general and specific information in simple texts on everyday familiar topics with or without visual support.
specific_standards: Reading: Comprehend short narratives about familiar experiences.
Reading: Extract specific information from texts on familiar topics.
Phonemic Awareness: Decode English graphemes and phonemes using knowledge of word parts, syllabification, and phonemic awareness.
learning_outcomes: Can comprehend short narratives about familiar experiences at a farm stand (e.g., "I go to the market and see some fruit.").
Can extract specific information from texts about farm products (e.g., "Papayas are on sale.").
Can decode English graphemes and phonemes, using knowledge of syllable segmentation (e.g., segmenting "banana" into "ba-na-na" with three syllables).

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can exchange personal information, descriptions of basic things, simple questions and answers, and simple directions.
specific_standards: Productive: Talk about people or things using simple language.
Interactive: Role-play simple social interactions.
learning_outcomes: Can talk about buying and selling things in familiar places (e.g., "Do you have any apples? I want to buy two." "Yes, I have some.").
Can role-play simple social interactions using polite language (e.g., "Can I have two mangos, please?").
Can ask questions about prices during role-play (e.g., "How much is this apple?").

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can create short, organized texts on familiar topics, incorporating revisions and feedback to improve clarity.
specific_standards: Productive: Create basic informational leaflets for the event.
Interactive: Write simple group summaries of chapters read in class.
learning_outcomes: Can create an informational leaflet describing farm stand items and prices for customers (e.g., "We have apples for one dollar and bananas for two dollars.").
Can write a simple summary of a story (e.g., "The story is about a farm stand. They sell fruits.").
Can tell classmates about the farm stand (e.g., "Come to our farm stand for fruit!").

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can utilize simplified language, visual aids, and step-by-step explanations to help peers engage with tasks and information.
specific_standards: Communication: Assist peers in following multi-step school procedures.
Concept: Explain the steps to solve a problem using practical examples.
learning_outcomes: Can assist peers in following multi-step school procedures by acting out steps (e.g., mimes "Next, pay for your fruit.").

Can guide peers through solving simple problems by modeling steps, using clarifying questions, and providing feedback (e.g., "First, choose fruit." and points to a fruit picture, then asks, "Which fruit do you want?" and provides feedback, "That's a great choice. What's next?").
Can summarize instructions for peers, using visuals or simple keywords (e.g., points to each item on a checklist and says, "Step one, step two…").

grammatical_features: Polite requests (e.g., "Can you help me, please?")
WH-questions (e.g., "How much is...?")
"Some" and "any" with countable/non-countable nouns (e.g., "Do you have any apples?" "I would like some water.")

linguistic_competences.nouns: mango, pineapple, guava, tomato, pepper, lettuce, papaya, banana, fruit, farm, egg, cheese, bread, vegetable, milk, sugar, salt, water, market, cashier, price
linguistic_competences.verbs: need, buy, sell, cost, ask, choose, want, give, get
linguistic_competences.adjectives: cheap, fresh, ripe, delicious, healthy, a lot, a few, some, many

vocabulary.pronunciation_and_phonemic_awareness: Pronunciation: /p/ in "papaya" and /b/ in "banana". Phonemic awareness: Segmenting words in syllables (e.g., "banana" to " ba-na-na" has three syllables).
vocabulary.pragmatic_competences: Asking about prices: "How much is this?" Asking about availability: "Do you have any...?" Describing availability: "We have some..." "I don't have any..."
vocabulary.sociolinguistic_competences: Discussing prices: Using polite expressions and transactional language at a farm stand (e.g., "How much is this basket of apples, please?").

skills_and_technology_integration.skills: Communication: Asking and answering questions about prices and quantities. Critical thinking and collaboration: Describing food and produce in role-play scenarios.
skills_and_technology_integration.technology_integration: Use apps or digital tools to create shopping lists and price lists.

projects.name: Project 1: Farm Stand Role-Play
projects.overview: Students participate in a role-play simulating a farm stand transaction, using polite requests and WH-questions (e.g., "How much is the pineapple?" "I need two papayas, please.").

projects.name: Project 2: Farm Stand Price List
projects.overview: Students create a price list for a simulated farm stand, using quantities and the present simple tense for items and prices.

projects.name: Project 3: Digital Shopping List
projects.overview: Students develop a simple shopping list with pictures, using a digital tool or sketching the app on paper. They practice quantifiers and polite requests to complete the list.

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can show comprehension of general information, specific information and instructions in short oral texts about daily events if spoken slowly and clearly.
specific_standards: Receptive: Demonstrate comprehension of the main points of extended discussions on familiar topics.
Interactive: Engage in role-plays based on familiar social situations.
learning_outcomes: Can demonstrate comprehension of the main points of extended discussions about household chores (e.g., "What do you do at home?" "I wash the dishes every day.").
Can engage in role-plays based on familiar social situations involving household responsibilities (e.g., "I clean my room on Saturdays.").
Can summarize key points about daily chores from discussions (e.g., "Everyone has chores at home.").

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can extract general and specific information in simple texts on everyday familiar topics with or without visual support.
specific_standards: Reading: Identify main ideas on familiar topics in simple paragraphs.
Reading: Illustrate main ideas from readings.
Phonemic Awareness: Decode English graphemes and phonemes using knowledge of word parts, syllabification, and phonemic awareness.
learning_outcomes: Can identify the main ideas in simple paragraphs about household chores (e.g., "Everyone helps with chores.").
Can illustrate main ideas from readings about helping at home, through drawings or discussions (e.g., "I help wash the dishes.").
Can identify open and closed syllables in simple words (e.g., "do" as an open syllable and "cook" as a closed syllable).

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can exchange personal information, descriptions of basic things, simple questions and answers, and simple directions.
specific_standards: Productive: Describe favorite hobbies or activities briefly.
Interactive: Exchange information about hobbies with peers.
learning_outcomes: Can describe a favorite household chore or activity using simple sentences (e.g., "I like cooking with my mom." "My favorite chore is watering the plants.").

Can have a simple discussion by asking and answering questions about chores and activities they do at home (e.g., "Do you help clean the house?" "Yes, I clean my room." "What chore do you like?" "I like doing the dishes.").
Can explain how they do simple chores at home using basic sentences (e.g., "I sweep and mop the floor every day." "I wash the dishes and then dry them.").

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can create short, organized texts on familiar topics, incorporating revisions and feedback to improve clarity.
specific_standards: Productive: Develop short poems or rhymes.
Interactive: Summarize feedback from peer reviews.
learning_outcomes: Can write a short poem or rhyme about household chores using simple vocabulary and repetition (e.g., "I sweep the floor, I wash the plate, I clean the room, I can't be late!").
Can write a simple summary of peer feedback on a classmate's poem or rhyme about chores (e.g., "Maria's rhyme was fun. She used good words and talked about cleaning the house.").
Can organize peer feedback into simple categories (e.g., what they liked, "Good job: used rhyming words." and what can be improved, "Needs work: add more lines about chores.").

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can utilize simplified language, visual aids, and step-by-step explanations to help peers engage with tasks and information.
specific_standards: Text: Simplify textbook content for peers.
Concept: Use visual aids to explain basic concepts.
learning_outcomes: Can simplify content on chores for their peers, using simple words and pictures (e.g., "Cleaning is making things tidy." while showing a tidy room image).
Can use visual aids to explain household chores (e.g., points to a clean room picture for "cleaning").
Can help classmates understand chores, using gestures (e.g., mimes sweeping for "We sweep.").

grammatical_features: Present simple (e.g., "I wash." "He washes." "I don't like to wash the dishes.")
WH-questions ( e.g., "What do you do at home?" "How often do you clean?")
Frequency adverbs (e.g., every day)

vocabulary.pragmatic_competences: Asking about chores: "What do you do at home?" Sharing experiences: "I help my mom."

skills_and_technology_integration.skills: Responsibility: Describing household chores. Communication: Explaining personal routines and chores in written and spoken forms.
skills_and_technology_integration.technology_integration: Use digital scheduling tools and apps to create a list of house chores for each family member.

projects.name: Project 1: Chore Scheduling App
projects.overview: Students create a digital schedule or use a paper scheduler for household chores. They describe daily routines, using the present simple tense (e.g., "I wash the dishes every day."), and frequency adverbs like "always" and "sometimes".

projects.name: Project 2: Family Chore Poster
projects.overview: Students design a chore poster showing who is responsible for different household tasks. They use the present simple tense and vocabulary for chores (e.g., "wash," "clean," and "sweep").

projects.name: Project 3: Chore Mural
projects.overview: Students each create a picture for a large classroom mural that shows various chores being completed.

scenarios.title: Time for Exercise
themes: I Like Walking in the Afternoon.

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can show comprehension of general information, specific information and instructions in short oral texts about daily events if spoken slowly and clearly.
specific_standards: Receptive: Comprehend the gist of short stories and news items.
Interactive: Engage in simple discussions on lessons or current events.
learning_outcomes: Can comprehend the gist of short stories about exercise (e.g., "The story is about a group of friends who play sports.").
Can participate in simple discussions about different types of exercises (e.g., "What exercises do you like?" "I like to swim.").
Can summarize the gist of news items related to health (e.g., "This news is about being healthy.").

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can extract general and specific information in simple texts on everyday familiar topics with or without visual support.

Can decode English graphemes and phonemes by segmenting words into parts, identifying syllables, and applying phonemic awareness (e.g., decoding "wellness" as "well-ness" and "exciting" as "ex-cit-ing").

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can exchange personal information, descriptions of basic things, simple questions and answers, and simple directions.

learning_outcomes: Can talk about people, using simple descriptions (e.g., "My friend can swim.").

Can discuss homework assignments with peers by offering or requesting help and following up with clarifying questions (e.g., "I need help with my physical education homework." "I can help you with the instructions." "What part do you need help with?").
Can ask classmates about their homework (e.g., "What is the homework for our physical education class?").

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can create short, organized texts on familiar topics, incorporating revisions and feedback to improve clarity.
specific_standards: Productive: Compose messages to invite peers to a performance, event, or activity.

themes: We Recycle Plastic Bottles Every Day.

Reading: Identify themes in simple stories.

Can identify themes in simple recycling-related stories and provide examples or connections from the story (e.g., "The story is about saving the Earth because the characters recycle bottles and plant trees.").
Can segment and decode multisyllabic words into syllables (e.g., dividing "environment" into "en-vi-ron-ment").

standards_and_learning_outcomes.general_standard: Can exchange personal information, descriptions of basic things, simple questions and answers, and simple directions.
specific_standards: Productive: Give a simple report based on a chart.
